title: unDraw illustration library (Katerina Limpitsouni)
lede: A free library of flat vector scenes whose accent color the user can change, named by Wired as one of the image banks that spread the style.
summary: Free flat vector scenes with one changeable accent color. A main source of the style on startup sites. Documented.

evidence.note: Read the unDraw license page and the Wired article. No illustration was downloaded, because the license forbids automated downloading without consent.

styles.note: Documented fit: Wired names unDraw with Freepik and Adobe’s library as image banks that let non-illustrators use the style. The illustrations were not inspected for this record.

context: The license page says the images may be used free for commercial and non-commercial purposes without credit, but may not be redistributed in packs, used to build a competing service, or used for machine learning, and that the license does not extend to automated scraping or downloading. [unDraw license](https://undraw.co/license).

Wired (24 January 2021): “Image banks such as FreePik, UnDraw, and Adobe’s own vector art library, have played a massive part in letting non-illustrators co-opt the Corporate Memphis style for themselves.” [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/corporate-memphis-design-tech/).
